name: Wix
description: Read-only Wix REST access to one site: site properties, Stores catalog products and eCommerce orders

tools.name: get_site_properties
tools.description: Get the connected Wix site's own properties (display name, business name, currency, time zone, locale and contact details)

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List products in the site's Wix Stores catalog (read-only catalog query), most relevant fields only

offset.description: Optional number of products to skip, for paging past the first page

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: List the site's Wix eCommerce orders, newest first, with payment and fulfillment status (read-only order search)

needs_review: Tools written 2026-09-12 from the official Wix REST reference: Site Properties V4 Get Site Properties (tools_source), Stores Catalog V1 Query Products (https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v1/catalog/query-products) and eCommerce Orders Search Orders (https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce/orders/orders/search-orders). All three are write:false.

list_products and list_orders are POST, which is Wix's shape for a READ: the two operations are CatalogReadApi.QueryProducts (documented permission WIX_STORES.READ_PRODUCTS) and Orders.SearchOrders (documented permission ECOM.READ_ORDERS). The verb is POST only because the query/search object rides in the body; neither mutates. The write flag stays false on both, so the shape-proof harness fires them without --include-writes.

Scaffolded auth is UNCHANGED (the raw API key in the Authorization header, no Bearer prefix), matching the vault registry's live-tested testHeaders for 'wix'. static_headers adds wix-site-id from the site_id credential field, which the official auth article requires verbatim: "an API key isn't bound to a single site, so each request must also identify its target: send a wix-site-id header for site-level calls or a wix-account-id header for account-level calls, but not both" (https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/rest-authentication/rest-api-authentication).

test.path was MOVED off the scaffolded /site-list/v2/sites to /site-properties/v4/properties. Evidence, curl 2026-09-12: /site-list/v2/sites answers 302 to https://users.wix.com/signin?... with an API key in Authorization, because it is an ACCOUNT-level call and the vault holds no account id, only site_id; /site-properties/v4/properties answers a structured 401 {"message":"MetaSiteId was not found on request","details":{"applicationError":{"code":"META_SITE_NOT_FOUND"}}}. The registry entry (services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js, key 'wix') still points its testEndpoint at the account-level path: not changed here, flagged.

Shape-proof 2026-09-12 (proofs/wix.proof.json): SHAPE_PROVEN on all 4 calls. /site-properties/v4/properties 401 {"message":"MetaSiteId was not found on request",..."code":"META_SITE_NOT_FOUND"}; /stores/v1/products/query 401 {"message":"No Metasite Context in identity.",..."code":"UNAUTHORIZED"}; /ecom/v1/orders/search 403 {"message":"read order: permission denied",..."code":"READ_ORDER_FORBIDDEN"}; control bogus path on the same host 404 with an EMPTY body. Caveat: every /stores/v1/* path answers that SAME 401 identity error (verified by curl against /stores/v1/collections/query and /stores/v1/products/{id}), so within that namespace the proof rests on the control differential rather than on a path-specific error.

Payload field names come from the documented schemas, NOT from a live 2xx: no Wix site was held for this draft. products picks priceData.* (the documented Product price block) rather than convertedPriceData, whose value depends on the caller's currency context. Order picks priceSummary.total.formattedAmount, the documented Price envelope field.

Catalog V1 is expressed, not Catalog V3: /stores/v3/products/query answered 403 with an EMPTY body under a dummy key, so its route cannot be blind-proved, while V1 answers a structured 401. Catalog V1 QueryProducts is documented GA with paging.limit maximum 100, which is the clamp cap used here. A V3 migration is an owner decision, not a blind one.

No filter or sort inputs: both Wix query objects take Wix Query Language filter structs, which an agent cannot be trusted to compose blind against a customer catalog. Paging only (limit, offset for products; cursorPaging.limit for orders, documented default 100). Search Orders also omits PENDING and REJECTED orders by default, per its own docs note: that default is left in place.
category set to 'commerce_finance' to match the shipped taxonomy (stripe, shopify, paddle). The scaffolded 'ecommerce' is not one of the 12 shipped buckets.
